KEY MESSAGE 1...

One final day with overcast skies to start the day given the
persistence of ample low and mid-level moisture. As our
positively tilted ridge builds overhead this afternoon, clouds
should finally lift and give way to some breaks of sun. The
peeks of sun, weak southerly flow, and warm air mass aloft 
should also help temperatures rise into the upper 60s to low 70s
this afternoon. With dew points still elevated in the upper 50s
this evening, partial clearing lingering into the evening 
should support fog development, especially in valley areas.
However, clouds look to increase overnight as a weak shortwave
tracks overhead and flattens the ridging aloft which should 
keep fog patchy. An expansive closed ridge parked over the 
Southeast U.S looks to build northward heading into Thursday, 
sending a warm front northward through the Northeast. Sufficient
warm air and moisture advection look to occur to not only 
increase cloud coverage on Thursday but also support some 
scattered showers in the southwest Adirondacks and western 
Mohawk Valley given topographical enhancements. The increased 
cloud coverage means temperatures on Thursday have trended 
slightly lower with latest NBM probabilistic guidance showing 
only a 40 - 60% chance for highs to exceed 75 degrees. 
Regardless, high temperatures in the 70s for early October are 
still above normal and elevated dew points will also make it 
feel a bit muggy. Continued cloud coverage Thursday night will 
keep temperatures warm with medium to high confidence that 
overnight lows remain above 60 degrees, again well above 
normal.

The warm mass continues into Friday as a cold front slides 
south and eastward from southern Canada into the Northeast. 
Latest trends suggest this will be an ana front with the
wind shift boundary occurring on the leading edge of the 
incoming rain. A rich moisture plume out of the Gulf 
characterized with PWATs 3 to 3.5 standard deviation above 
normal per the NAEFS becomes directed around the northern 
periphery of the aforementioned ridge in the Southeast U.S and 
focuses along the incoming ana cold front. The boundary tracks 
from northwest to southeast Thurs night into Friday. Showers 
initially look to remain hung up in the southwest Adirondacks
for a few hours Fri morning before a shortwave from the Ohio 
Valley pushes eastward and helps nudge the cold front eastward.
There is increasing confidence that the most widespread showers
arrive Friday afternoon and while rain should fall steady for a
period, the fast flow aloft likely keeps it progressive with 
most rain ending by Fri evening. NBM probabilistic guidance 
still shows only a 15-30% chance for 24hr rainfall amounts 
through 2AM Saturday to exceed 0.50" for most of eastern NY and 
western New England. The exception is southern VT and the 
southwest Adirondacks where there is a 50 to 75% chance that 
rainfall amounts exceed 0.50" due to upslope enhancements. Very 
low probabilities for rain amounts to exceed 1 inch means 
flooding is not anticipated.


KEY MESSAGE 2...

After a stretch of near to above normal temperatures late this 
week into the weekend, there is increasing confidence for a push
of chilly air to overspread the region early next week. After a
cold front marches through on Monday, an expansive area of high
pressure from the Central Plains builds eastward ushering in
below normal temperatures. There is strong consensus among 
ensemble guidance that temperatures Monday night and especially
Tuesday night given favorable set-up for radiational cooling
allowing temperatures to turn quite cool. There is a 30 to 60% 
chance that temperatures fall to or below 35 degrees in valley 
areas where the growing season in still ongoing (focused in the 
Hudson Valley). Highest confidence for the lowest temperatures 
and potential frost formation remains in Hudson Valley areas 
north of Albany.
